newsitem.title: CROATIA: CROATIAN INTERBANK RATES RISE, DEMAND POOR.
newsitem.headline: CROATIAN INTERBANK RATES RISE, DEMAND POOR.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates were somewhat higher on Wednesday in quiet trade, money market dealers said.
"It's been a very quiet day on the money market with banks repaying some 30 million kuna and some 20 million remaining on offer by 0830 GMT," dealer Jasenka Blagaic told Reuters.
Fresh deals were put at just 12.5 million kuna and mostly consisted of call money loans granted at a steady 7.0 percent.
One-month interbank deals were made at 14 percent, up two percentage points.
Savings banks paid 15 percent for one-month money, up from Tuesday's 14 percent.
Insurers were charged 9.0 percent for one-month deals.
Banks' balances dropped slightly to 563 million kuna and banks had some 4 million kuna in outstanding Lombard loans.
One bank reported a shortfall of 18.5 million kuna which equalled Tuesday's overnight trade. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
